issues.detail: The Hebrew 'יִשָּׂא בְשִׂיחִי מִשְׁכָּבִי' means 'my couch will carry/ bear my complaint' (i.e., my bed will take up my complaint), but the Chinese renders it as '我的言語必扶起我的床' ('my words will lift up my bed'), reversing the subject and object: the Hebrew subject is 'my couch/bed' (מִשְׁכָּבִי) and the object is 'my complaint' (שִׂיחִי), whereas the Chinese makes 'my words' the subject and 'my bed' the object. This changes who is doing what to whom.
